This matches a bug we keep hitting. We run opencode headless (`opencode run --format json`) to benchmark Bedrock models, and the assistant's final text gets dropped: `execute()` returns as soon as `prompt()` resolves, before the loop drains the final `text`/`step-finish`/`idle` events, so the in-process server tears down mid-flush. This PR's `await` fixes it. Minimal repro: ask for `58 + 71` and you get empty stdout on `dev`, `129` with this PR. Confirmed across several Bedrock models.

It's actually a re-regression: #26955 added this await, then #27371 dropped it while reworking exit handling (moved the exit code onto `result.error` and detached the loop again).

On testing: the `run-process.test.ts` happy-path assertion passes even on the un-awaited code, because the in-process TestLLMServer delivers events fast enough that the detached loop wins the race. So a non-empty-stdout assertion isn't a sufficient guard; catching this needs latency injected before the final events so a detached loop deterministically loses.

One small suggestion: early-returning on `result.error` before the await avoids a hang if a request never starts a run (e.g. an unknown command, which never emits idle).

We hit the Bedrock side of this. Meta's Llama models on Bedrock reject tool use over `/converse-stream` (`ValidationException: This model doesn't support tool use in streaming mode`), so with tools they're unusable today. `streaming: false` fixes it: verified against real Llama 4 Maverick, which then made native tool calls and answered correctly, with streaming models unaffected (Claude on Bedrock still streamed, `test/session/llm.test.ts` green).

One Bedrock-specific gap I ran into: the prompt-transform middleware only runs for `args.type === "stream"`, so under `doGenerate` the Bedrock message transform gets skipped. Widening that guard to also run when streaming is off makes the Bedrock path correct under `streaming: false`. Happy to send a patch against this branch.

This issue might be a duplicate of existing issues. Please check:
- #21737: Custom `@ai-sdk/anthropic` provider loads correctly but drops API key at runtime when using custom baseURL — nearly identical symptoms: bundled provider used, API key not propagated, same log line `using bundled provider`, blank/401 responses
- #5674: Custom OpenAI-compatible provider options not being passed to API calls — same root cause category: provider options (including `apiKey`/`baseURL`) not forwarded to bundled SDK provider
- #15756: SDK `session.prompt()` returns empty responses with custom OpenAI-compatible provider — same observable symptom of empty responses with custom provider despite direct API calls working

Closing as duplicate of #21737, #5674, and #15756. Same root cause: bundled SDK provider not forwarding apiKey/baseURL to third-party providers like FreeModel. API works via curl but opencode returns blank/empty responses because provider options are not propagated to the bundled @ai-sdk/anthropic and @ai-sdk/openai-compatible packages.

I can confirm this also affects FreeModel (third-party Anthropic/OpenAI compatible provider).

In v1.16.2, when configuring FreeModel with custom baseURL and apiKey:
- @ai-sdk/anthropic with custom api: response received but content is blank (no error logged)
- @ai-sdk/openai-compatible with custom api: 403 Unauthorized (API key not sent)

API works perfectly via curl with both endpoints. The bundled SDK providers do not propagate the configured apiKey/baseURL to the actual HTTP requests.

+1 on treating Kiro as a first-class provider instead of forcing custom config.

A minimal path that would be useful:

- provider entry in `/connect`
- env fallback via `KIRO_API_KEY`
- conservative `/models` list until Kiro exposes stable metadata
- docs note for plan/subscription/API-key availability

For testing, it might also help to keep the implementation provider-agnostic enough that people can validate against a hosted Kiro-compatible/API-backed endpoint as well as local CLI headless mode. Disclosure: I’m involved with https://kiroforge.cloud, which could be useful as one optional test target, but the OpenCode integration should definitely stay cleanly configurable rather than tied to any specific service.

Closing as a duplicate of #31204 — same SQLite error, same appendMessage → session.next.agent.switched path, same root cause (no seq on insert). This was filed from macOS 26 (Homebrew opencode 1.15.13), no plugins, so the trigger condition is more general than originally reported.

Adding a second reproduction + workaround confirmation from macOS 26 (Apple Silicon), Homebrew-managed opencode 1.15.13 in /opt/homebrew/bin, no plugins:

**Reproduction (macOS 26, no plugins, model=opencode-go/minimax-m3):**

```
$ opencode run --model opencode-go/minimax-m3 --dir "$PWD" --dangerously-skip-permissions "echo hello"
Error: { "name": "UnknownError", "data": { "message": "Unexpected server error.", "ref": "err_c822fa6f" } }

# Server log:
ERROR service=server ref=err_c822fa6f error=NOT NULL constraint failed: session_message.seq
  at appendMessage (chunk-9re0szbd.js:2:62522)
  at session.next.agent.switched (chunk-9re0szbd.js:2:56643)
  at SessionPrompt.createUserMessage
```

Identical stack to the report above, but the trigger was the very first `opencode run` prompt — no agent switching was required. The same `appendMessage` path is reached on initial session creation.

**Two co-existing installs on this host:**
- /opt/homebrew/bin/opencode -> opencode-ai@1.15.13 (npm, broken)
- /Users/chaos/.opencode/bin/opencode -> 1.16.2 (standalone, working)

**Workaround that worked:** use the canonical 1.16.2 binary at `$HOME/.opencode/bin/opencode` (the path the upstream install script chooses per the README's priority 4). No DB migration or wipe was needed; the existing migrated schema was honored by the newer runtime and `session_message` rows started inserting normally.

So: confirmed on a clean install with no plugins, the same root cause (CLI 1.15.x does not populate `seq` for the new projection migrations), and the same operational fix (upgrade the CLI to the same family that wrote the migration).

PR created: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/31428
Three changes in prompt-input.tsx:

handleInput now guards during composition — skips events while composing, except insertReplacementText and insertText (Gboard autocomplete events that arrive after compositionend)
handleCompositionStart cancels stale rAF — prevents a lingering compositionEnd callback from interfering with a new composition
handleCompositionEnd reconcile checks isPromptEqual — only re-renders from model if DOM has actually diverged, preventing the double-reconcile race condition

> We hit the Bedrock side of this. Meta's Llama models on Bedrock reject tool use over `/converse-stream` (`ValidationException: This model doesn't support tool use in streaming mode`), so with tools they're unusable today. `streaming: false` fixes it: verified against real Llama 4 Maverick, which then made native tool calls and answered correctly, with streaming models unaffected (Claude on Bedrock still streamed, `test/session/llm.test.ts` green).
> 
> One Bedrock-specific gap I ran into: the prompt-transform middleware only runs for `args.type === "stream"`, so under `doGenerate` the Bedrock message transform gets skipped. Widening that guard to also run when streaming is off makes the Bedrock path correct under `streaming: false`. Happy to send a patch against this branch.

Feel free to send it, thanks for testing!👍
